paraphrase: Mounting to mind-only, one should not imagine an external object; abiding in the object that is suchness, one should pass beyond mind-only; passing beyond mind-only, one should pass beyond the imageless; the yogin abiding in the imageless sees the Mahāyāna. The effortless state is peaceful, purified by vows; the supreme selfless wisdom is not seen in the imageless.

paraphrase: Is the stream of what is seen as one's own mind purified gradually or all at once? Gradually — as mangoes ripen, pots are made, grasses grow and arts are learned step by step; and also all at once — as a mirror shows all forms at once, the sun and moon light all forms at once, the ālaya displays its world at once, and the dharmatā-buddha shines at once.

paraphrase: Mahāmati asks whether the tathāgatagarbha — described as luminous, pure, within all beings, permanent, covered by the aggregates — is not the same as the self taught by the tīrthikas. The Buddha answers that it is not: the Tathāgatas teach the tathāgatagarbha meaning emptiness, the reality-limit, nirvāṇa, the unborn, the signless and wishless, so that the foolish may not fear no-self; bodhisattvas should not cling to it as a self.
